doc.title: Writing Tests
doc.paragraph: This section goes over how to add tests that afwdev test will run. Tests belong with the source they cover, under each source directory's tests folder. This is not a tutorial on Adaptive Script itself. It is about the layout and metadata the test runner expects.

section.title: Where Tests Live
section.paragraph: Under each source directory:
section.code: src/<srcdir>/tests/ some_group/ # ordinary test group (one or more files) foo.as bar.as afw.conf # optional; used when the group needs conf objects/ # optional fixtures config.py # optional Tags, Environment, before/after hooks environments/ # optional shared fixtures (named; see config.py) models/ afw.conf …
section.paragraph: The afwdev test command walks src/*/tests/ and can be limited with --srcdir-pattern and --test-pattern. A group is usually a directory of related files that should stay together when they share conf or data. A short note about the core gate tree is in src/afw/tests/README.md.

section.title: Running Tests
section.paragraph: From the package root, after you have made code or generate changes, build with ./afwdev build --cdev and then run tests with afwdev on your PATH. Use ./afwdev when the build must refresh afwdev itself. Use afwdev afterward for test, validate, and similar.
section.code:
# From package root — after code/generate changes ./afwdev build --cdev -j
# Run tests (installed afw / afwfcgi on PATH) afwdev test -j afwdev test --srcdir-pattern afw --test-pattern 'rql/.*' afwdev test --list --test-pattern smoke

section.title: Kinds of Tests
section.paragraph: The following table describes the kinds of tests the runner understands:

row.column: The usual choice. Language, functions, and adapters under optional afw.conf.
When you need host process control, raw environment octets, or bindings that are awkward in script.
Drive shell-ish command sequences with a special runner.
Multi-request or long-lived afwfcgi work with orchestration.yaml. See Orchestrated Tests below.

section.paragraph: You will usually want to use a test script unless you need process lifetime, a private server, or host-only APIs.

section.title: Adaptive Test Scripts
section.paragraph: Most tests are Adaptive test scripts. These are .as files compiled with --syntax test_script. A file starts with a shebang that names afw and test_script, then one or more cases described by //? metadata lines.

The shebang must mention afw and test_script, as above or as afw --syntax test_script. Metadata lines start with //?. Keys such as test, description, expect, source, and skip are the common ones. Failures are reported per test: case.

Multi-line values use //? key: ... and then the text on the following lines until the next //?, or the end of the file. That form keeps the text more literally, including newlines inside the block. A blank line before the next //? is the usual way to keep a final newline on the last content line.

File values use //? key: <<< relative/path, with the path relative to the directory of the .as file. The file contents become the key's value exactly, with no trim. Paths must be relative and must not contain .. segments. This is useful for long expects or sources. A value that starts with <<< is always this form, so do not begin a free-text description with those characters. After //? source: ... or //? source: <<< …, the body is the multi-line or file form above.

The expect key is usually Adaptive source for the return value you want, for instance 0, true, "ok", anyURI("…"), or undefined. It is not free text. The runner compiles and evaluates that source and compares it to the result of the case. A <<< file for expect must contain that Adaptive source. For instance, put quotes around "hello" if you want a string return value.

Two reserved tokens are not Adaptive values. The token success means the case compiled and ran without throwing. The result is ignored. The token error, or error: followed by a message, means the case should throw.

Optional keys expect-stdout and expect-stderr assert the text written to the Adaptive stdout and stderr streams during the case, for instance by print, println, or stream writes. These values are literal strings, not Adaptive source. They use the same forms as other keys: same-line trim, ..., or <<<. Comparison is exact utf-8. Use a hyphen in the key name. Do not put a colon inside the name. expect:stdout is wrong, because : separates the key from the value. When these keys are present, the harness captures output into an in-memory buffer so it does not pollute the afw process result channel. Omit the key to ignore that stream.

If the script needs adapters or other conf, put afw.conf in the same directory, or use a shared tests/environments/<name>/ and set Environment in config.py. The default --env-mode afw runs afw with that conf when the group provides it. Keep fixtures small and hermetic. The runner copies group files into a temporary work directory.
A group may define:

list.item: Tags — a list of strings. afwdev test --tags with a regular expression filters groups.
Environment — the name of a directory under tests/environments/.
before_all, after_all, before_each, and after_each — hooks.

section.paragraph: See existing config.py files under src/afw/tests/ for patterns. The easiest way to start is to copy a nearby test and edit it. For instance, look at src/afw/tests/language/script/try.as and src/afw/tests/compiler/test_script_file_value/.

section.title: How afwdev test Runs Tests
section.paragraph: The --env-mode option chooses how the runner hosts each test:

row.column: A subprocess afw for .as files. Hermetic orchestrated-test leaves spawn afwfcgi.
.as files under valgrind. Orchestrated leaves wrap afwfcgi when that is supported.

Replays compatible .as files against a live stack. The default URL is http://localhost:8080/afw. Tests with a private afw.conf are skipped. Orchestrated leaves are also skipped, because hermetic conf does not apply to the live process.
A local Python Session and eval_script for .as files.

section.paragraph: The file type still wins for some paths. A .py file uses the Python runner. A commands_*.txt file uses the commands runner.

section.title: Orchestrated Tests
section.paragraph: Use an orchestrated leaf when you need a long-lived afwfcgi, leaf-local conf, multi-request checks, REST feeds, Accept overrides such as application/x-afw, or a firehose schedule. Firehose replaces the retired afwdev blast subcommand. The leaf is a directory that contains orchestration.yaml. See src/afw/tests-extra/README.md and the gate examples under src/afw/tests/advanced/.
The same vocabulary applies where it makes sense: expect, expect-stdout, expect-stderr, plus expectResponse and expectStatus for wire bodies.

Leaves under src/afw/tests/ are part of the default gate that afwdev test -j runs. Keep those short. Leaves under src/afw/tests-extra/ are opt-in extras next to tests/ for soaks, progressive work, firehose, and sketches. Those run only when you pass -T. Schema and extra scenarios live in src/afw/tests-extra/README.md.
section.code: src/afw/tests-extra/<leaf>/ # or tests/<group>/ for gate leaves orchestration.yaml # or orchestration.json (not both) afw.conf objects/ # optional fixtures tests/ or *.as # payloads (sourcePath / <<<)

version: 1 host: afwfcgi description: Short summary afwfcgi: threads: 1 timeout_s: 60 feed: # defaults for every test kind: action accept: application/json tests: - name: first sourceType: script source: | return true; expect: true - name: progressive feed: accept: application/x-afw # override default Accept only sourceType: script sourcePath: tests/to_response.as # optional schedule: sequential | parallel | firehose | repeat

list.item: A document-level feed supplies defaults. A per-test feed overrides fields.
sourceType together with source, sourcePath, or <<< path is the same idea as evaluating a test script.
expect is an optional JSON-ish compare of the action result. Test script payloads use the inner passed flag.
schedule.firehose takes duration, concurrency, maxRequests, and fromTests for load.
This requires PyYAML and afwfcgi on PATH from an install build.

section.code: afwdev test --capture-goldens -T path/to/leaf # or: AFWDEV_CAPTURE_GOLDENS=1 afwdev test -T path/to/leaf
section.paragraph: That writes the actual response bytes to each expectResponse: <<< rel/path. Re-run without capture for the gate.

section.title: Some Practical Advice

list.item: Start from a neighbor. Copy a test in the same area and edit it.
Name files so --test-pattern is useful. Patterns match the file path, the basename, or the leaf directory name for orchestration markers.
Keep groups small. Shared conf is fine. Do not hide unrelated suites in one directory if you want fine-grained parallel runs.
After meaningful changes, run afwdev test -j. Valgrind mode is slower and optional for day-to-day work.
Many function and datatype scripts under tests/generated/ are generated. Prefer hand tests under clear group names for new product behavior.
Put load and soak work in orchestrated leaves with firehose under src/afw/tests-extra/, or under other -T roots. Do not put heavy firehose in the default tests/ gate.

section.paragraph: Maintainer notes for the orchestrated schema are in src/afw/tests-extra/SCHEMA.md. Command help is available from afw --help (-s test_script) and afwdev test --help.
